Class TextInputElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<TextInputElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.TextInputElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class TextInputElement extends StyledElement<TextInputElement>
A DSL wrapper for the TextInput widget.

A single-line text input field. This element is always focusable to receive keyboard input for text editing. 

textInput(inputState)
    .placeholder("Enter name...")
    .title("Name")
    .rounded()

CSS Child Selectors

The following child selectors can be used to style sub-components:

  • TextInputElement-cursor - The cursor style (default: reversed)
  • TextInputElement-placeholder - The placeholder text style (default: dim)

Example CSS: 

TextInputElement-cursor { text-style: reversed; background: yellow; }
TextInputElement-placeholder { color: gray; text-style: italic; }

Note: Programmatic styles set via cursorStyle(Style) or placeholderStyle(Style) take precedence over CSS styles.

    • isFocusable

      public boolean isFocusable()
      Returns whether this text input is focusable.

      By default, text inputs are focusable to receive keyboard input. Use focusable(boolean) to disable focusability for display-only inputs.

      Specified by:
      isFocusable in interface Element
      Overrides:
      isFocusable in class StyledElement<TextInputElement>
      Returns:
      true if focusable (default), false if disabled via focusable(boolean)

    • focusable

      public TextInputElement focusable(boolean focusable)
      Sets whether this text input is focusable.

      By default, text inputs are focusable. Set to false for display-only inputs that should not participate in TAB navigation or receive keyboard events. This is useful when the text input is used to display read-only data within a container that handles its own key events.

      Overrides:
      focusable in class StyledElement<TextInputElement>
      Parameters:
      focusable - true to make focusable (default), false to disable
      Returns:
      this element for chaining
      See Also:
      • for more details on focusability

    • cursorRequiresFocus

      public TextInputElement cursorRequiresFocus(boolean requiresFocus)
      Sets whether the cursor requires focus to be displayed.

      When true (default), the cursor is only shown when this element is focused. When false, the cursor is shown whenever showCursor(boolean) is true, regardless of focus state. This is useful when the text input is inside a focusable container that handles key events manually.

      Parameters:
      requiresFocus - true to require focus for cursor display
      Returns:
      this element for chaining

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size

      public Map<String,String> styleAttributes()
      Description copied from interface: Styleable
      Returns the style attributes for attribute selector matching.

      Attribute selectors like Panel[title="Test"] match elements based on their style attributes. This method returns a map of attribute names to their values.

      Common attributes include:

      • title - the element's title
      • label - the element's label
      • placeholder - the element's placeholder text
